newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: UK's Rifkind sees no change in EMU policy.
newsitem.headline: UK's Rifkind sees no change in EMU policy.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind denied on Monday that Prime Minister John Major was considering changing policy on the European single currency.
Speaking at a news conference at the OSCE meeting in Lisbon, he said: "I have no reason to believe it is going to change."
British officials said Rifkind was speaking immediately after talking to Major, who is also attending the OSCE meeting.
The officials also dismissed suggestions that Major was considering a change of policy, saying the government's position was clear and remained unchanged.
The Daily Telegraph reported on Monday that Major had concluded it would be against Britain's interests to join a single currency in the next Parliament.

The newspaper, with good sources in the ruling party, said Major was seeking to persuade Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke to agree to ditch the current "wait-and-see" policy before the looming general election.

Major, lagging Labour in opinion polls, is being put under pressure by ruling Conservatives opposed to European integration -- so-called Eurosceptics -- to rule out entry into a single currency in the life of the next parliament.
